I was curious as to how a rather specialized language would evolve. Basically, any idiot can form a contraction with two words and an even lesser idiot can pick up the saying. Sign language seems like it would be much more difficult to disseminate especially prior to the rise of multimedia being shared on the internet. It's obviously less static than say Morse code so I suppose I was just wondering how the language evolved. Is there a group which decides which movements become words or can anyone introduce a new word so long as it catches? How are the new words spread to other speakers? I'm obviously observing with at least some bias but it just strikes me as a massive undertaking with incredibly difficult logistics which is worthy of understanding. I suppose I have always wanted to have greater interaction with deaf people simply to understand what is really a very different experience. I've also always wondered what deaf people "heard" when reading subtitles representing an abstract sound. Do they make up something in their head or just acknowledge the thing makes a sound and forget about it? I'm not trying to be a dick, I'm genuinely curious about their experience.
